task.title: Example Shopping
task.shortdesc: A worked example of shopping for components

taskbody.context: The second step in building a desktop is to find and purchase your build components

step.cmd: I go to LogicalIncrements and look for a build set that roughly totals out to $1,000. This is the ‘Great’ category. I won’t use these suggestions exactly, but they are a good place to start looking.

image.alt: an example build suggestion from LogicalIncrements.com

step.cmd: I decide to buy online rather than go to Micro Center.
I then go to PCPartPicker and click on Start Your Build in the middle of the page.

I go through each category and pick parts roughly in line with my budget. I know the GPU will be the most expensive part of the build, followed by the CPU and motherboard. I want all my parts to be roughly in the same performance tier, so for a $250 GPU I want an approximately $200 CPU and motherboard.

image.alt: an example shopping list from PCPartPicker.com

step.cmd: I decide on getting an additional SSD to go with my old HDD so my new system isn’t bottlenecked by old slow storage. I will install my OS and any games on the SSD while all my music stays on my HDD.
The peak power draw for the system is estimated at 409W. I selected a 750W PSU for better efficiency.
My total comes to $908.84. I could either be satisfied or see if I can find a few more dollars to get a new monitor for my new graphics card.
